newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Workers reject jobs plan at steelmaker Clabecq.
newsitem.headline: Workers reject jobs plan at steelmaker Clabecq.

text.p: Workers at bankrupt Belgian steelmaker Forges de Clabecq on Thursday rejected a take-it-or-leave-it early retirement package, throwing into doubt a possible takeover by an Italian firm.
The package, among other things, covers early retirement, the problem of workers over 50 and the allocation of money made on the sale of stock.
On Wednesday militant union leader Roberto D'Orazio poured cold water on the package, describing it as "peppered with traps", and on Thursday the workers unanimously rejected it.
There have been a number of clashes between police and the steelworkers since the firm was declared bankrupt in January.
On Thursday D'Orazio called for a "decisive" demonstration on May 3.
The Walloon Region, Clabecq's majority shareholder, put forward the package on Monday following talks with unions, Clabecq's court-appointed receivers and federal ministers.
The plan aims to alleviate the consequences of bankruptcy for the workers and make the company attractive for a takeover.
Several firms have been mentioned in connection with a possible buyout, but to date the only one to have actually declared an interest is Italian steel and commodity trader Duferco.
